title: Requirement for Manufacturers of Health Supplements to Provide Test Results from Accredited Laboratories to Support Advertising Claims
what_it_is: Requirement for Manufacturers of Health Supplements to Provide Test Results from Accredited Laboratories to Support Advertising Claims

sections.label: Health supplement advertising rules
sections.summary: Health supplements support well-being, not disease prevention or treatment; disease claims are banned, with fines up to $5,000 or two years' imprisonment, and mandatory testing is not being considered.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Health supplements are used to support general well-being, and not for the purposes of preventing or treating diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Dealers are allowed to use authoritative reference texts, such as official publications issued by authorities and published literature, to support and substantiate their product claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This approach to advertising claims for health supplements is similar to those adopted in the United States, Australia, Canada and Japan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, advertisements on health supplements which claim to prevent or treat diseases are not allowed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Non-compliant advertisers may face a maximum penalty of a fine of up to $5,000 or imprisonment up to two years or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Mandatory testing by dealers to back up advertisement claims, therefore, is not being considered at this time.

sections.label: Post-market surveillance of health products
sections.summary: HSA conducts post-market surveillance, using a risk-based approach to sampling health products and testing them for toxic heavy metals and prohibited ingredients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In addition, Dr Chia Shi-Lu speaks of the post-marketing surveillance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, there is a post-market surveillance that monitors the safety of these products as they hit the shelves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, HSA takes a risk-based approach to identifying what this sampling of the health products would take, what scope it would cover, and also takes an active step in looking at this in sampling, to test them for toxic heavy metals and other prohibited ingredients.

sections.label: Guidelines legislation plans
sections.summary: The speaker does not rule out turning the guidelines into legislation, but says there are no plans to do so at this point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Whether or not these guidelines should eventuate into legislation, I would not rule that out but, at this point in time, there are no plans to do so.
